stem: Why are bleach baths recommended for some patients with atopic dermatitis?

options.text: To bleach the skin and reduce erythema
To decrease Staphylococcus aureus colonisation and its inflammatory effects
To chemically break down thick scales and lichenification
To increase the penetration of topical corticosteroids applied immediately after
To dry out weeping lesions by removing all skin moisture

explanation: Decreasing Staphylococcus aureus colonisation is the main reason for bleach baths in atopic dermatitis, as this can reduce bacterial-driven inflammation and disease flares.
rationale: Bleach baths are used for their antimicrobial effect rather than for cosmetic skin changes or scale removal.

optionExplanations.A: Incorrect because bleach baths are intended to reduce bacterial burden and inflammation, not to whiten the skin.
optionExplanations.B: Correct because bleach baths help reduce Staphylococcus aureus colonisation on the skin and lessen its inflammatory effects in atopic dermatitis.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because bleach baths are not used to chemically remove thickened skin or lichenification.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because any effect on topical steroid absorption is not the main reason bleach baths are recommended.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because bleach baths are not used to deliberately desiccate lesions by removing skin moisture.

source.hint: Consider the role of 'golden staff' in the skin's inflammatory process.
